ai.description: *Liurana alpina* is a tiny frog (15–18 mm) with a mottled brown dorsum and pale venter. It is distinguished by a prominent, fleshy papilla on the tongue and reduced toe webbing.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Liurana alpina* is best distinguished from similar congeners by the presence of a distinct, fleshy, conical papilla on the dorsal surface of its tongue.
ai.habitat: *Liurana alpina* inhabits high-altitude alpine meadows and rocky streams in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 3,500 and 4,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Liurana alpina* is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among the high-altitude rocky scree and mossy habitats of the Himalayas during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Liurana alpina* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in mossy, semi-aquatic habitats. Its development is direct, bypassing a free-living tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Liurana alpina* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of Arunachal Pradesh in Northeast India, typically occurring at elevations between 3,000 and 4,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Liurana alpina* consists of a series of high-pitched, pulsed chirps emitted from hidden positions within high-altitude rocky stream habitats.
